transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I’m scared by how I eat sometimes. Once I start, especially alone in the kitchen, it feels like I can’t make myself stop. I’m telling myself, “Janet, put it away,” but it’s like I’ve stepped aside and I just keep going.
After these episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit?
No, I don’t make myself vomit afterward.
After these eating episodes, do you ever do anything to try to make up for them, like taking laxatives?
I’m not really sure what you mean by making up for them. I feel bad afterward, but… I don’t know.
After you overeat like that, do you ever take laxatives?
I’m not sure. I mean, I feel bad after, but I don’t really know what counts as trying to make up for it.
After these eating episodes, do you take laxatives?
I’m honestly not sure. I know I feel upset afterward, but I don’t really know what you mean by that.
After you eat this way, do you ever take laxatives?
I don’t know—I haven’t really thought of anything I do afterward in those terms.
After these eating episodes, do you ever fast by skipping meals on purpose?
I’m not really sure. Do you mean deliberately not eating the next meal because of what I ate?
Yes—do you ever skip your next meal on purpose after one of these eating episodes?
I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve really paid attention to whether I skip the next meal on purpose.
After one of these eating episodes, do you deliberately exercise extra to burn off the calories?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed myself doing extra exercise after eating.
When this happens, do you eat what most people would consider a very large amount of food in a short period of time?

Yes. Some afternoons, like after a food bank shift or baking for a senior-center event, I’ll get home and have a full plate of leftovers, then banana bread, chips, cheese, and cookies from the tin. Afterwards I realize it was much more than I’d serve anyone else for a meal.
During these eating episodes, do you feel unable to stop or control how much you’re eating?
Yes. Once I start, especially if I’m alone in the kitchen, it feels like I can’t make myself stop. I’m telling myself, “Janet, put it away,” but I just keep eating. It’s scary.
After these eating episodes, do you ever do something on purpose to prevent weight gain?
I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed myself doing anything deliberately afterward to try to make up for it.
Do these eating episodes upset you a lot?
Yes, a lot. Afterwards I feel awful about myself—like I wasted food I meant to share, and I’m too old to be acting this way. I just sit there ashamed and promise myself it won’t happen again.
